issues: Verification date 2026-08-19 postdates my knowledge cutoff — cannot confirm the status claims or the installation state described

Tools 'remindctl' and 'imsg' from steipete/tap are unverifiable from my training data (may be newer than my cutoff, or fabricated); 'memo' from antoniorodr/memo appears to be a real, recent Apple Notes CLI
Permission path cited as 'System Settings → Privacy' — renamed to 'Privacy & Security' since macOS Ventura; minor outdated UI reference
Document truncated at 2000 chars — the iMessage permission section is cut off mid-sentence and remaining content (e.g., full references list) could not be reviewed
'brew tap X && brew install X/Y/Z' is redundant — modern Homebrew allows direct 'brew install X/Y/Z' (cosmetic, not deprecated)
AppleScript usage is still supported (not deprecated), but no mention of JXA or macOS Sequoia/Tahoe automation-permission prompt changes that affect first-run behavior

The documented API does not match Anthropic's official computer-use tool, which uses actions like screenshot/mouse_move/left_click with coordinate-based input (computer_20241022 / computer_20250124 / GA Claude 4 tooling); action names like 'capture', 'element=N', 'capture_after', and 'mode=som' describe a custom or third-party harness that cannot be verified from the doc

Claim 'There is no Anthropic-native schema to learn' is misleading/outdated — a native, versioned computer-use tool schema has existed since Oct 2024 and is now GA; the skill should clarify it targets a non-Anthropic harness

Claim that 'Claude was trained on both' element indices and coordinates is unverifiable; Anthropic's public computer-use training is screenshot+coordinate based, and SOM/AX index overlays come from the tool at runtime, not model training — this may cause models to over-trust index clicking

No tool version, harness repo, or macOS version is pinned; AX role names (AXButton, AXTextField) and background-automation permissions (Accessibility + Screen Recording grants, Sequoia's permission re-prompts) vary across macOS releases, so the AX-index approach can silently rot

No URLs present in the excerpt, so dead links could not be checked, but the absence of any link to the tool's source or docs makes the skill unverifiable and harder to keep fresh
